Variants.Content: Strongsong is the seat of House Belmore, set among the valleys and hills of the northern Vale. The 'song' in its name carries the ancient cadence beloved by nobles of the Vale, while the surrounding terrain is thoroughly practical: mountain torrents, narrow glens, pastures, and roads leading inland decide who can come and who can leave. House Belmore ranks among the major bannermen of the Vale, obliged both to take part in the ceremonies and levies of the Eyrie's order and to handle local troubles such as mountain clans, grazing disputes, and winter road closures. This place is far from the splendor of King's Landing, and very close to stone, snow, and silence.
Entry Strongsong Local families also rely on goats, thin fields, orchards, and pack teams crossing the Mingyue Mountains; if any road, well, or dock fails, the price falls first on them.

Entry Strongsong They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the valley; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Strongsong If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.
Entry Strongsong A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Strongsong They care about goats, thin fields, orchards, and pack teams crossing the Mingyue Mountains. They also look at whether seeds are left after collecting grain, and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
